subject: Request: OpalWorks availability/latency variance for launch
messages:
From: Alex Reed <alex@opalworks.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Launch ask — committed latency + availability for OpalWorks GA

Hi Mina / Marissa,

We’re planning a staged GA for OpalWorks on 2027-03-28 and we need Redwood to sign up to a stronger availability and latency commitment for a limited period during launch week and the subsequent 90-day ramp. High level: expected baseline QPS 4k, burst up to ~18k sustained for 10–30 minutes during marketing pushes.

Concrete ask: a temporary variance that commits to 99.95% monthly availability and a p95 inference latency target of <100ms for production traffic during the first 90 days, with a path to a permanent Dedicated reservation after that. We understand this is aggressive — happy to take tradeoffs (credits, reserved capacity, pre-launch testing).

Attached: opal-launch-requirements.pdf (traffic profile + end-to-end SLIs). Can we get a quick internal decision cadence so we can align commercial terms?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call this afternoon.

— Alex
Alex Reed
Head of Platform, OpalWorks
alex@opalworks.com

(attachment: opal-launch-requirements.pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex@opalworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Launch ask — committed latency + availability for OpalWorks GA

Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Looping in Sales (Marissa) and our account-level ops lead (Sean) so we can coordinate product/eng feedback and commercial terms. A few initial clarifying questions from product/infra so we scope the engineering impact: 

- Can you confirm the expected p95 calculation windows (end-to-end vs inference-only)?
- For the 18k burst, is that across a single region or multi-region? Do you expect geo-shifts?
- Any PII or regulated workloads in the GA traffic?

Prelim plan from my side: we can evaluate a time-boxed variance (90 days) if we get: 1) Dedicated reserved capacity sizing commitment, 2) pre-launch stress test with your traffic replay, and 3) agreement on operational playbooks (on-call, runbooks). I attached a short runbook template to capture requirements.

Propose a 30-minute sync Monday to triage.
— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
(attachment: MVP_runbook_template.docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Reed <alex@opalworks.com>, Sarah Park <sarah.park@opalworks.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Feb 2027 08:19:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Launch ask — committed latency + availability for OpalWorks GA

Thanks Alex — adding a couple commercial notes so product/engineering sees the full ask:

- OpalWorks is asking for a launch-week SLA uplift and 90-day variance to support their marketing calendar. They’re willing to commit to a Minimum Reserved Capacity (we’ve discussed an initial 3-month commit).
- Customer expects credits if commitments are missed. They’ve asked for language that is symmetrical to a standard SLA credit policy but with higher p95 promises during the ramp.
I’ve started a mutual action plan (attached) and linked the HubSpot record here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/opalworks/record/OW-2237. If product & eng can outline the acceptable operational caveats we’ll push commercial terms and DocuSign.
(attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx)

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Reed <alex@opalworks.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed carveout approach for OpalWorks (need ENG signoff)

Team — based on the ask, here’s a proposed carveout path to review: 

1) Approved variance window: 90 days post-GA (launch week + ramp)
2) Commitment: 99.95% monthly availability (service reachable) and p95 inference latency target <100ms for production inference requests representing 85–90% of traffic.
3) Conditions: Dedicated reserved capacity sized to their burst profile (initial estimate: 30% headroom over baseline capacity), mandatory pre-launch stress test with replay, and an operational runbook + on-call rota during ramp.
4) Credits: tiered credits if commitments are missed (commercial to finalize).
I’ve attached a redline template for SLA clauses (proposed_sla_redlines.pdf). From Sales ops side, this is doable if Engineering confirms the reserved sizing approach and Product accepts the risk profile.
Please add technical constraints / acceptance criteria — Karthik, can you review and confirm the feasible p95 target and the capacity assumptions?
(attachment: proposed_sla_redlines.pdf)

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Account Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Reed <alex@opalworks.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed carveout approach for OpalWorks (need ENG signoff)

Thanks — quick technical summary and constraints from infra/serving: 

- p95 <100ms inference-only is achievable for the majority of model calls if: 1) requests are served from a single model family variant optimized for low-latency (quantized 8-bit variant), 2) KV cache warming is in place, and 3) we enforce request size limits (max tokens).
- Burst profile: sustained 18k QPS in a single region will require reserved Dedicated capacity with autoscale thresholds tuned; our preliminary capacity calc says ~120 GPU-vCPU units (see attached capacity_calc_sheet.xlsx). Without Dedicated reservation, we can’t guarantee the p95 target during sustained bursts — risk of graceful degradation to a higher-latency model variant.
- Operational asks: 48-hour runbook handover, a single-point traffic replay feed for the stress test, and a restricted blackhole plan (ability to throttle marketing traffic if we observe systemic non-linear failure modes).
- Risk: if client traffic has a heavy tail of long-context requests or sudden geo-shifts, p95 will spike. We recommend making the SLA explicit about the traffic profile tested and excluding outlier windows caused by customer-side misconfiguration.
Attaching our inference runbook outline and the capacity calc. If Sales accepts the Dedicated sizing and the customer signs a reserved commit, Engineering can sign off on the 90-day variance. Otherwise we need to offer a conditional SLA tied to reserved capacity and a larger credit band.
(attachment: capacity_calc_sheet.xlsx)
(attachment: inference_runbook.md)
— Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex@opalworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, legal@opalworks.com
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Decision: Temporary variance approval path for OpalWorks (next steps)
Alex — thanks again for the detailed requirements and for being flexible on implementation. We ran this with infra/product/legal and can offer the following path: 

1) Redwood will approve a 90-day availability/latency variance conditioned on: a signed 3-month Dedicated reserved capacity commit (sizing consistent with Karthik’s calc), a successful pre-launch stress test with traffic replay, and formal runbook handover.
2) SLA language will include an explicit traffic profile appendix (what we tested) and a capped credit schedule for missed commitments. Legal will send a DocuSign with the redlined clause by EOD tomorrow: https://redwood.example/docusign/OW-SLA-2237
3) Operational readiness: we need the traffic replay feed by 2027-03-10 and a pre-launch 4-hour stress window with Redwood observers. If the stress test fails to meet the agreed p95 threshold, we’ll either increase reserved capacity or shift to a mixed-variant fallback (which will be documented in the appendix).
Marissa — please finalize the mutual action plan and commercial credits. Karthik — please confirm the final reserved sizing after the replay data arrives; we’ll need a runbook sign-off 7 days prior to GA.
Alex — once legal has the signed DocuSign we’ll schedule the replay and run the stress test. Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting OpalWorks across the line.
— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
(attachment: none)

Appreciate the fast turnaround — we’ll coordinate replay details with Karthik and Marissa.
— Alex
Alex Reed
